expectations.text: A preregistration document exists that states hypotheses, a numeric acceptance threshold, and fixed measurement conditions
expectations.evidence: outputs/PREREGISTRATION.md (mtime 05:58:39) states H1 ('median per-unit time of C_regex > median of C_find by at least 10% (R = median(t_regex)/median(t_find) >= 1.10) with sign-flip p < 0.05'), H0, H2 (12/12 consistency), a 'Fixed objects' table, and section 2 'Fixed conditions - NOT changed after start' (interpreter, read path, exact per-line tests, unit-of-3, warmups, N=12, shuffle seed 20261121, GC protocol, no-interim-looks).

expectations.text: The preregistration (and its frozen copy) mtime <= mtime of the confirmatory measurement data (main-matrix raw records, e.g. runs.jsonl). Pilot or eval-set generation files may precede the freeze by design.
expectations.evidence: os.path.getmtime: PREREGISTRATION.md 2026-11-21 05:58:39 and docs/find-vs-regex/PREREGISTRATION_frozen.md 05:58:43, both <= data/run_main.jsonl 05:59:45 (main-matrix raw records). Pilot files (data/pilot_runs.jsonl 05:57:38, test_log_50mb.log 05:56:47) precede the freeze, which is allowed by design; the pilot was find-only so no regex timing preceded the freeze.

expectations.text: Raw per-run records were saved (individual runs in jsonl/csv files), not only summary statistics
expectations.evidence: data/run_main.jsonl contains 26 raw records (24 units + 2 warmups), each with ts_utc, cond, repeat, warmup, passes, per-pass times ('pass_times_s': [0.1635093, 0.1660935, 0.1628348]), elapsed_s, and matched_counts; data/pilot_runs.jsonl and data/run_order.json also saved. Report section 11 confirms 'Raw per-unit records: data/run_main.jsonl (26 lines: 24 units + 2 warmups)'.

expectations.text: The final report states effect size AND variance (mean +/- std or CI), not just the best single run
expectations.evidence: report.md section 1-3: effect R = 1.2318 (median unit 0.669 s find vs 0.824 s regex), 95% percentile bootstrap CI of R [1.2217, 2.2277], p = 0.000488, per-unit spread (find min 0.355 / median 0.669 / max 0.676, MAD_rel 0.0099; regex min 0.484 / median 0.824 / max 0.832, MAD_rel 0.0019), all 12 paired differences listed (0.016-0.471 s). Not a single best run.

expectations.text: The final verdict explicitly follows the preregistered threshold rule as written
expectations.evidence: Prereg section 5 verdict rule: 'if R >= 1 + thr and p < 0.05: VERDICT = "H1 confirmed - ADOPT str.find in the pipeline"'. Report section 1: 'H1 confirmed - ADOPT str.find in the pipeline (looked up from the frozen rule, not argued): R = median(t_regex)/median(t_find) = 1.2318 >= 1 + 0.10, with sign-flip p = 0.000488 < 0.05'. The verdict string matches the preregistered mapping exactly and cites both gate conditions; analysis_results.json 'verdict' field contains the identical string.

expectations.text: The decisions registry (DECISIONS.md) shows append-order integrity: row timestamps are non-decreasing, and any decision claiming to precede measurements is supported by file mtimes or artifact manifest hashes, not only by its own text
expectations.evidence: DECISIONS.md rows D-001..D-008 are non-decreasing: 00:56, 00:57, 00:58, 01:00, 01:01, 01:01, 01:02, 01:04 UTC. D-003 (00:58 UTC) claims the freeze precedes the main matrix; independently supported by mtimes (PREREGISTRATION_frozen.md 05:58:43 local = 00:58:43 UTC < run_main.jsonl 05:59:45 local = 00:59:45 UTC) and by sha256: recomputed hash of both PREREGISTRATION.md and the frozen copy is 146a6dc842223200f2a370e88bd9e69299ff4a9cc50fa8ee350459844e58441f, exactly the hash D-003 records. Also, ts_utc values inside run_main.jsonl (00:59:29-00:59:45 UTC) are after the freeze time.

expectations.text: Total wall time stayed within approximately 10 minutes (treat as satisfied if executor duration <= 700 seconds, from timing.json)
expectations.evidence: timing.json: total_duration_seconds = 912.7 (duration_ms 912685), which exceeds the 700-second cutoff.

claims.claim: One find unit was an outlier at 0.355 s 'vs siblings ~0.66-0.68 s'
claims.evidence: analysis_results.json t_find_s shows FOUR units below 0.5 s (0.355, 0.366, 0.368, 0.372) plus one at 0.477, not a single outlier among ~0.66-0.68 siblings. The report's post-hoc narrative understates the spread; does not affect the median-based verdict, but the description is inaccurate.

suggestions.assertion: Total wall time stayed within approximately 10 minutes
suggestions.reason: The 700 s cutoff is checked only against timing.json, which the harness writes; the expectation is about process discipline, not artifact content, so it can fail a methodologically excellent run for a reason the executor's outputs cannot influence (this run did everything else right and still fails 1/7). Consider reporting it separately from the method-quality expectations or bumping the budget.

No assertion checks that the numbers in the report match the raw records. Here the report's post-hoc section misdescribes the find-time distribution (calls 0.355 s 'one outlying unit' when four units were < 0.5 s). A grader-only cross-check of report numbers against analysis_results.json/raw jsonl would catch narrative drift.

suggestions.assertion: The preregistration (and its frozen copy) mtime <= mtime of the confirmatory measurement data
suggestions.reason: mtime ordering is a good tamper check, but the frozen copy's hash equality with the working prereg (verified here via sha256) is what makes the freeze meaningful; consider making the hash-match part of the expectation text.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong run: prereg, freeze, raw records, variance reporting, and registry integrity all hold up under independent recomputation. Only wall time failed, and only because the executor exceeded 700 s while doing the full prereg pipeline.
